gettingStarted.title: Getting Started
gettingStarted.content:
Welcome to **Filarr Notes** — your personal knowledge management system built right into Filarr.

**Create your first note:** Click the **+** button in the Notes sidebar, or press `Ctrl+N`.

**Write freely:** The editor supports rich text, markdown shortcuts, slash commands, and more. Just start typing.

**Connect your knowledge:** Type `[[` to create wiki-links between notes, files, and folders. These connections build your personal knowledge graph.

**Daily journaling:** Press `Ctrl+Shift+D` to create (or open) today's daily note — perfect for journaling, stand-ups, or daily logs.

**Explore views:** Switch between List, Masonry, Kanban, Sticky Notes, Canvas, and Graph views using the view toggle bar at the top.

shortcuts.title: Keyboard Shortcuts
shortcuts.content:
**Navigation:**
- `Ctrl+N` — Create a new note
- `Ctrl+Shift+D` — Open/create today's daily note
- `Ctrl+Shift+G` — Toggle graph view
- `Ctrl+Shift+F` — Toggle focus mode (distraction-free writing)
- `Ctrl+P` — Open command palette

**Text Formatting:**
- `Ctrl+B` — Bold
- `Ctrl+I` — Italic
- `Ctrl+U` — Underline
- `Ctrl+Shift+X` — Strikethrough
- `Ctrl+Shift+H` — Highlight text

**Editor Shortcuts:**
- `/` — Open slash command menu
- `[[` — Insert wiki-link with autocomplete
- `#` at start of line — Heading (## for H2, ### for H3)
- `-` or `*` at start — Bullet list
- `1.` at start — Numbered list
- `[]` at start — Task/checkbox
- `>` at start — Blockquote
- `---` — Horizontal rule
- ` ``` ` — Code block

interfaceOverview.title: Interface Overview
interfaceOverview.content:
The Notes interface is divided into three main areas:

**Left Panel — Notes List:**
- Browse, search, sort, and filter your notes
- Create new notes, daily notes, or notes from templates
- Pin important notes to keep them at the top
- Access Flashcards, Templates, and this Wiki

**Center — Editor:**
- Rich text editor powered by TipTap
- Floating bubble menu for quick formatting (select text to see it)
- Toolbar at top with formatting, focus mode, version history, and export
- Breadcrumb trail showing recently visited notes
- Slash commands (`/`) for inserting blocks

**Right Panel — Backlinks & Smart Tags:**
- See which notes link to the current one (backlinks)
- Discover potential unlinked mentions
- View outgoing links
- Get AI-suggested tags based on content analysis

bubbleMenu.title: Floating Bubble Menu
bubbleMenu.content:
When you **select text** in the editor, a floating toolbar appears with quick formatting options:

- **Bold**, **Italic**, **Underline**, **Strikethrough**
- **Code** (inline monospace)
- **Highlight** with color picker (8 colors available)
- **Link** insertion

The bubble menu follows your selection and disappears when you click away. It's the fastest way to format text without leaving the keyboard.

slashCommands.title: Slash Commands
slashCommands.content:
Type `/` at the beginning of a new line to open the **slash command menu**. Available commands:

**Text blocks:**
- `/heading1`, `/heading2`, `/heading3` — Section headings
- `/paragraph` — Normal text

**Lists:**
- `/bulletlist` — Unordered list
- `/orderedlist` — Numbered list
- `/tasklist` — Checkboxes / to-do list

**Content:**
- `/blockquote` — Quote block
- `/codeblock` — Code with syntax highlighting
- `/table` — Insert a table
- `/horizontalrule` — Divider line
- `/image` — Embed an image
- `/file` — Embed a file from your library

Start typing after `/` to filter commands. Press Enter or click to insert.

highlightColors.title: Highlight Colors
highlightColors.content:
Filarr Notes supports **multicolor highlighting** — perfect for color-coding different types of information.

**How to use:**
- Select text and click the highlight button in the bubble menu or toolbar
- Choose from 8 preset colors: yellow, green, blue, purple, pink, red, orange, gray
- Click the same color again to remove the highlight

**Use cases:**
- **Yellow** for key takeaways
- **Green** for action items
- **Blue** for references and sources
- **Red** for warnings or critical items
- **Purple** for ideas and brainstorming

focusMode.title: Focus Mode
focusMode.content:
**Focus mode** removes all distractions so you can concentrate on writing.

**Activate:** Press `Ctrl+Shift+F` or click the focus icon in the toolbar.

**What changes:**
- The sidebar and backlinks panel are hidden
- The editor takes up the full screen
- Non-active paragraphs are slightly faded to help you focus on the current block

**Exit:** Press `Ctrl+Shift+F` again or click the exit button in the toolbar.

Focus mode pairs well with the **Writer** editor theme for a distraction-free writing experience.

dragDropBlocks.title: Drag & Drop Blocks
dragDropBlocks.content:
Rearrange content blocks by dragging them:

**How it works:**
- Hover over any block (paragraph, heading, list, etc.) — a **drag handle** (6 dots) appears on the left
- Click and hold the handle to start dragging
- Drop the block at a new position — a blue insertion line shows where it will land

**Supported blocks:**
- Paragraphs, headings, blockquotes
- Lists (entire list or individual items)
- Code blocks, tables
- Embedded files and images

This makes it easy to reorganize your notes without cutting and pasting.

editorThemes.title: Editor Themes
editorThemes.content:
Customize the editor's look and feel with three built-in themes:

**Default** — Clean, balanced design with the standard Filarr look.

**Writer** — Optimized for long-form writing:
- Serif font (Georgia) for comfortable reading
- Warm cream-tinted background
- Wider line spacing
- Centered, narrower text column

**Developer** — Designed for technical notes:
- Monospace font (JetBrains Mono / Fira Code)
- Dark-friendly styling
- Better code block contrast

**Switch themes:** Use the theme selector dropdown in the editor toolbar. Your choice persists across sessions.

wikiLinks.title: Wiki-Links
wikiLinks.content:
**Wiki-links** are the core of the knowledge graph. They connect your notes bidirectionally.

**Create a link:** Type `[[` and start typing a name. The autocomplete shows:
- **Notes** — your existing notes
- **Files** — documents in your library (use `[[file:document.pdf]]`)
- **Folders** — your folder structure (use `[[folder:Projects]]`)

**How links work:**
- Clicking a wiki-link opens the linked note
- `Ctrl+Click` opens the linked note in a split panel
- Links are bidirectional — if Note A links to Note B, Note B shows a backlink to Note A

**Link syntax:**
- `[[Note Title]]` — Link to a note
- `[[file:filename.pdf]]` — Link to a file
- `[[folder:FolderName]]` — Link to a folder
- `![[Note Title]]` — Embed (transclude) a note inline

backlinks.title: Backlinks & Auto-Links
backlinks.content:
The **Backlinks Panel** (right side of the editor) shows all connections to the current note:

**Backlinks** — Notes that explicitly link to this note via `[[wiki-links]]`. Shows a context snippet around each mention.

**Outgoing Links** — Notes, files, and folders that this note links to.

**Potential Links** (Auto-detected) — Other notes that mention this note's title in their text but haven't created an explicit link yet. Click the "+" to convert a mention into a link.

**Orphan Detection** — Notes with no incoming or outgoing links are flagged with an orange "unlinked" badge in the notes list, helping you discover disconnected knowledge.

transclusion.title: Transclusion (Note Embedding)
transclusion.content:
**Transclusion** lets you embed the content of one note inside another.

**Syntax:** Use `![[Note Title]]` (note the exclamation mark before the brackets).

**What happens:**
- The referenced note's content appears inline as a bordered, read-only card
- The embedded content updates live — edit the source note and the transclusion refreshes
- Click the transclusion to navigate to the source note

**Use cases:**
- Create a "dashboard" note that aggregates sections from multiple notes
- Reuse definitions, templates, or reference material across notes
- Build a master document from modular components

breadcrumb.title: Breadcrumb Navigation
breadcrumb.content:
The **breadcrumb trail** appears above the editor, showing the last notes you visited.

- Up to **10 recent notes** are tracked
- Click any breadcrumb to jump back to that note
- The trail resets to the current note when you navigate
- Useful for quickly switching between related notes you're working on

The breadcrumb is your "back" button for note navigation — no need to search for notes you just had open.

hoverPreview.title: Link Preview on Hover
hoverPreview.content:
Hover over any `[[wiki-link]]` in the editor to see a **preview popover** without leaving the current note.

The preview shows:
- Note title
- First ~150 characters of the note content
- Word count and link count
- Last updated date

This lets you quickly check what a linked note contains before deciding to navigate to it.

splitEditing.title: Split Note Editing
splitEditing.content:
Open two notes side by side:

**How:** Hold `Ctrl` and click a wiki-link. The linked note opens in a new panel to the right.

This uses Filarr's tab system — you can have multiple notes open in separate tabs and split panels.

**Use cases:**
- Compare two notes
- Reference material while writing
- Copy content between notes
- Review linked notes without losing your place

listView.title: List View
listView.content:
The default view — a traditional **sidebar + editor** layout.

**Left sidebar shows:**
- All notes sorted by date, title, or word count
- Search bar to filter notes instantly
- Sort controls (Modified, Title, Created, Words) with ascending/descending toggle
- Note count
- Pinned notes appear at the top

**Right side:** The full editor with toolbar, bubble menu, and backlinks panel.

**Tip:** Pin frequently accessed notes to keep them at the top of the list regardless of sort order.

masonryView.title: Masonry View
masonryView.content:
**Pinterest-style card grid** showing all your notes as cards.

Each card displays:
- Note title
- First ~100 characters of content preview
- Word count and link count
- Cover color (if set)
- Daily note badge

Cards are arranged in a responsive masonry layout that fills available space. Click any card to open it in the editor.

**Best for:** Visual overview of all notes, quickly scanning content, finding notes by appearance.

kanbanView.title: Kanban View
kanbanView.content:
Organize notes into **columns** — perfect for project management and workflows.

**Default columns:** Inbox, In Progress, Review, Done.

**Features:**
- **Drag & drop** notes between columns to change their status
- **Add columns** — click "+" to create custom columns
- **Delete columns** — hover a column header and click the trash icon
- Notes are automatically saved to their column

**How it works internally:** The column assignment is stored in the note's metadata, so moving between columns is instant.

**Best for:** Project tracking, content pipelines, task management, sprint planning.

stickyNotesView.title: Sticky Notes View
stickyNotesView.content:
A **free-form 2D canvas** where notes appear as colored sticky notes.

**Controls:**
- **Drag** a sticky note to reposition it
- **Scroll wheel** to zoom in/out
- **Shift+click** and drag on the background to pan the canvas
- Notes snap to a 20px grid for clean alignment

**Colors:** Each note gets a color from the palette (yellow, green, blue, purple, pink, orange). Colors cycle automatically.

**Best for:** Brainstorming, mind mapping, spatial organization, visual thinkers.

canvasView.title: Canvas / Whiteboard
canvasView.content:
An **infinite 2D whiteboard** that displays note cards with connection lines.

**Features:**
- Note cards show title, preview, and metadata
- **SVG connection lines** are automatically drawn between linked notes
- **Zoom** with scroll wheel or toolbar buttons (+, -, Reset)
- **Pan** with Shift+click and drag
- Zoom percentage displayed in toolbar

**Controls:**
- Click a card to open it in the editor
- Cards are positioned in a 4-column grid by default
- The connection lines follow wiki-links between notes

**Best for:** Visualizing note relationships, system design, project mapping.

graphView.title: Graph View
graphView.content:
The **Graph View** visualizes your knowledge as an interactive network.

**Node types:**
- **Circles** (blue) = Notes
- **Squares** (green) = Files
- **Hexagons** (yellow) = Folders

**Node size** reflects how many connections each item has.

**Interactions:**
- **Click** a node to select and open it
- **Drag** nodes to rearrange the layout
- **Scroll** to zoom in/out
- **Click + drag** on empty space to pan

**Edge types:**
- Solid lines = note-to-note links
- Dashed lines = note-to-file or note-to-folder links

The graph uses a real-time **force-directed layout** — nodes repel each other and edges pull connected nodes together.

graphClusters.title: Automatic Clusters
graphClusters.content:
Enable **Clusters** to automatically group densely connected notes.

**How it works:**
- Uses a simplified **Louvain algorithm** for community detection
- Notes that are heavily interconnected form a cluster
- Each cluster gets a unique color
- A legend shows all clusters with their colors

**Toggle:** Click the cluster icon in the graph toolbar (top-left, three-circle icon).

**Insights:** Clusters reveal hidden structure in your knowledge — topics you've written about extensively tend to form tight groups. Isolated clusters might indicate disconnected areas worth bridging.

graphHeatmap.title: Heat Map Mode
graphHeatmap.content:
Toggle the **heat map** to visualize note recency.

**Color coding:**
- **Red/Hot** — Recently edited notes (today/yesterday)
- **Yellow/Warm** — Edited this week
- **Blue/Cold** — Older, stale notes

**Toggle:** Click the flame/pin icon in the graph toolbar.

**Insights:** The heat map reveals which parts of your knowledge base are actively maintained and which areas might need revisiting. Cold clusters are opportunities for review.

Note: Clusters and Heat Map are mutually exclusive — enabling one disables the other.

graphFilter.title: Graph Filter
graphFilter.content:
Use the **search bar** in the graph toolbar to filter nodes by title.

**How it works:**
- Type a search term in the filter input
- Matching nodes remain fully visible
- Non-matching nodes fade to 12% opacity (they're still there, just dimmed)
- Edges to dimmed nodes also fade

**Use cases:**
- Focus on a specific topic area
- Find where a particular note sits in your knowledge graph
- Explore the neighborhood of a specific node

graphTimeTravel.title: Time Travel
graphTimeTravel.content:
The **Time Travel** slider lets you see your knowledge graph as it was at any point in time.

**How to use:**
- Click the clock icon in the graph toolbar to enable time travel
- A slider appears below the toolbar
- Drag the slider to scrub through time
- Notes created after the selected date are hidden
- The current date is displayed next to the slider

**Use cases:**
- See how your knowledge base has grown over time
- Review what you knew at a specific point
- Identify when connections were formed

templates.title: Templates
templates.content:
**Templates** provide pre-structured content for common note types.

**Built-in templates:**
- **Meeting Notes** — Attendees, agenda, decisions, action items
- **Decision Log** — Context, options considered, decision, rationale
- **Weekly Review** — Accomplishments, challenges, next week's goals
- **Brainstorm** — Topic, ideas, evaluation, next steps

**Using a template:** Open the Template Manager (grid icon in the sidebar), browse templates, and click "Use Template".

**Custom templates:** Open any note, then click "Save as Template" at the bottom of the sidebar. Your note's content becomes a reusable template.

**Variables:** Templates support `{{date}}`, `{{title}}`, and other placeholders that are automatically filled when you create a note from the template.

dailyNotes.title: Daily Notes
dailyNotes.content:
**Daily notes** are automatically dated journal entries — one per day.

**Create:** Press `Ctrl+Shift+D` or click the calendar icon in the sidebar.

**Naming:** Daily notes use the format "YYYY-MM-DD" (e.g., "2026-03-14").

**Smart carry-over:** When you create a new daily note, any **unchecked tasks** from the previous day's note are automatically carried over to the new note under a "Carried Over" heading. This ensures nothing falls through the cracks.

**Badge:** Daily notes have a calendar icon badge in the notes list to distinguish them from regular notes.

**Best for:** Daily journals, stand-up notes, work logs, habit tracking.

pinning.title: Pinning Notes
pinning.content:
**Pin** important notes to keep them at the top of the sidebar, regardless of sort order.

**How:** Click the pin icon on any note card, or right-click and select "Pin".

Pinned notes have a subtle pin badge and are always visible at the top of the list. This is useful for:
- Quick access to frequently referenced notes
- Keeping project dashboards visible
- Marking notes you're actively working on

sortingSearching.title: Sorting & Searching
sortingSearching.content:
**Search:** The search bar at the top of the sidebar filters notes instantly as you type. It searches both titles and content.

**Sort options** (click the sort icon to cycle):
- **Modified** — Most recently edited first (default)
- **Title** — Alphabetical order
- **Created** — Newest notes first
- **Words** — Longest notes first

**Sort order:** Click the arrow (up/down) to toggle ascending/descending.

**Note count:** The total number of matching notes is shown next to the sort controls.

smartTags.title: Smart Tags (AI Suggestions)
smartTags.content:
Filarr uses **TF-IDF analysis** to automatically suggest relevant tags for your notes.

**How it works:**
- The algorithm analyzes the text of all your notes
- It finds keywords that are **distinctive** to each note (common words across all notes are de-prioritized)
- The top 5 keyword suggestions appear below the Backlinks panel
- Supports both **English and French** stop word filtering

**Adding a tag:** Click the "+" button next to any suggestion to create and apply the tag to your note.

**TF-IDF explained:** Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency is a statistical measure that evaluates how important a word is to a document in a collection. Words that appear frequently in one note but rarely in others get higher scores.

orphanDetection.title: Orphan Detection
orphanDetection.content:
**Orphan notes** are notes with no incoming or outgoing wiki-links — they're disconnected from your knowledge graph.

**Identification:** Orphan notes display an orange dot badge in the notes list.

**Why it matters:** Orphaned notes represent knowledge that isn't connected to anything else. You might want to:
- Add wiki-links to connect them to related notes
- Check if they contain useful information worth linking
- Delete them if they're no longer needed

**Backlinks Panel:** When viewing an orphan note, the backlinks panel shows "No connections" and suggests creating links.

folderNotes.title: Notes in Folders
folderNotes.content:
Notes can be **associated with folders** in your file system, appearing alongside your files.

When notes are linked to a folder, they show up as compact cards in the Folder View, below the files section.

**Click** a note card in the folder view to open it in the Notes editor.

This bridges the gap between your document library and your knowledge system — meeting notes can live next to meeting files, project notes next to project documents.

versioning.title: Version History
versioning.content:
Filarr automatically saves **version snapshots** of your notes as you edit.

**How it works:**
- Snapshots are taken every **30 seconds** (minimum interval between versions)
- Up to **20 versions** are kept per note (oldest are pruned)
- Each version stores the full content, title, and word count

**Viewing history:** Click the **clock icon** in the editor toolbar to open the Version History panel.

**Features:**
- **Timeline** — Browse all saved versions with timestamps
- **Diff view** — Click "Show Diff" to see what changed between two versions (green = added, red = removed)
- **Restore** — Click "Restore" on any version to revert the note to that state

**Storage:** Versions are stored locally in your profile storage — they persist across sessions.

export.title: Multi-Format Export
export.content:
Export your notes in five formats:

**Markdown (.md)** — Clean plain text with formatting. Perfect for sharing, publishing, or migrating to other tools.

**HTML (.html)** — Fully styled web page. Includes Filarr's typography and can be opened in any browser.

**PDF (.pdf)** — Portable document. Good for printing or sharing formal documents.

**DOCX (.docx)** — Microsoft Word format. Ideal for collaboration with people who use Word.

**Filarr (.filarr)** — Complete backup including all metadata, wiki-links, tags, and version history. Use this for full backups or transferring between Filarr installations.

**How to export:** Click the **download icon** in the editor toolbar to open the Export dialog. Choose your format, toggle options (include metadata, include links), and click Export.

flashcards.title: Flashcards
flashcards.content:
Create **flashcards** from your notes for spaced repetition learning.

**Adding Q&A pairs:** Write questions and answers in your notes using these formats:

`Q: What is a wiki-link?`
`A: A bidirectional link between notes using [[brackets]]`

Or the shorter format:
`? Question here`
`! Answer here`

**Generating a deck:** Open the Flashcard view (card icon in the sidebar header), then click "Generate from Notes" to scan all your notes for Q&A pairs.

**Reviewing:**
- Cards show the question first
- Click "Reveal" to see the answer
- Rate your recall: Again, Hard, Good, or Easy
- The **SM-2 algorithm** schedules cards for optimal review intervals

**Spaced repetition:** Cards you find easy are shown less frequently. Cards you struggle with are shown more often. This scientifically optimizes your learning.

fileEmbed.title: File & Image Embedding
fileEmbed.content:
Embed files and images directly in your notes.

**Methods:**
- Use the slash command `/image` or `/file`
- Drag and drop a file from the Filarr file explorer into the editor

**Supported previews:**
- **Images** (PNG, JPG, GIF, SVG) — inline image preview
- **Videos** (MP4, WebM) — video player
- **Documents** (PDF, DOCX, etc.) — file card with icon and name

**File cards** show the file name, type icon, and size. Click a file card to open it in Filarr's file viewer.

This lets you create rich notes that combine text with visual and document references.

markdownShortcuts.title: Markdown Shortcuts
markdownShortcuts.content:
The editor recognizes common **Markdown syntax** and converts it to rich text automatically:

- `# Heading 1`, `## Heading 2`, `### Heading 3`
- `**bold**` → **bold**
- `*italic*` → *italic*
- `~~strikethrough~~` → ~~strikethrough~~
- `==highlight==` → highlighted text
- `\`code\`` → inline code
- `- item` or `* item` → bullet list
- `1. item` → numbered list
- `[] task` → task checkbox
- `> quote` → blockquote
- `---` → horizontal rule
- `\`\`\`` → code block

These shortcuts work inline as you type — no need to switch modes. The text is converted to rich content immediately.

fullTextSearch.title: Full-Text Search
fullTextSearch.content:
Filarr Notes uses **FlexSearch** for instant full-text search across all your notes.

**Features:**
- Search by content, title, or both
- Results appear as you type with highlighted snippets
- Prefix queries: type `title:keyword` to search only in titles
- Handles thousands of notes with sub-millisecond response times

**Where it's used:**
- The search bar in the Notes sidebar
- Wiki-link autocomplete (`[[`)
- Command palette

**Technical details:** The search index is built in-memory from your Redux store and updates automatically as you create, edit, or delete notes. It uses tokenized indexing for fast fuzzy matching.

tips.title: Tips & Best Practices
tips.content:
**Build connections gradually.** Don't worry about creating the perfect structure upfront. Add wiki-links as you write, and the graph will emerge naturally.

**Use daily notes as an inbox.** Capture thoughts in your daily note, then refine and link them to permanent notes later.

**Review orphans regularly.** Check the orphan badges in your notes list — these are notes that could benefit from connections.

**Use templates for recurring notes.** Meeting notes, weekly reviews, and project logs are perfect candidates for templates.

**Leverage the graph.** Switch to Graph View periodically to discover unexpected connections and identify knowledge gaps.

**Export for backup.** Use the Filarr (.filarr) export format periodically for a complete backup of your knowledge base with all metadata intact.

**Keyboard-first workflow.** Learn `Ctrl+N`, `Ctrl+Shift+D`, `/`, and `[[` — these four shortcuts cover 90% of note creation and linking.

import.title: Import Notes
import.selectSourceDesc: Choose the source to import your notes from.
import.obsidianDesc: Obsidian vault (.md with wiki-links and tags)
import.obsidianInstructions: Select the root folder of your Obsidian vault.
import.notionInstructions: In Notion: Settings → Export all content → HTML or Markdown format. Select the exported ZIP file.
import.evernoteInstructions: In Evernote: select notes → File → Export (.enex). Select the exported .enex file.
import.importTagsDesc: Creates tags found in the imported notes.

vaultLock.subtitle: Enter your vault password to unlock
